numerical_characteristics.precision: The issue discusses evaluating in floating point versus exact symbolic computation; the proposed floor uses evalf with precisions 10, 100, 1000 and the test value a(857) requires exact integer agreement, but no explicit float dtype is stated.
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: a(857) equals a 180-digit-plus exact integer (about 10^179 scale), as given by the 857th Fibonacci-digit-count value in the test.
category_specific_evidence: Reproducer: a(n) = int(2**n*log(phi)/log(10) - Rational(1,2)*log(5)/log(10)) + 1 with phi=(1+sqrt(5))/2, exact symbolic arithmetic via sympy Rational/log/sqrt.
Test asserts a(857) == a857 where a857 is an exact large integer literal beginning 200829212952178927690909380949249948846461002549293765663931 and ending ...585966267100.
Issue states that evaluating in floating point gives only an order of magnitude of the digit count rather than the exact number of digits, so int/floor must be exact.

Issue suggests a floor routine iterating evalf precision 10, 100, 1000 and checking i <= x < i+1 to certify the correct floor; warns x could be within 1e-300 of an integer and then fail with an exception.
Patch in Expr.__int__ adds: if int_valued(r): r = self.round(15); i = int(r), a higher-precision retry when the float-rounded value looks integral.
PR describes it as a partial fix making int(expr) use more robust numeric evaluation and avoid slower symbolic simplification.
reproduction_risks: Result depends on near-integer behaviour: the value may lie extremely close to an integer, so 15-digit rounding in the patch may be insufficient; the issue itself notes risk within 1e-300 of an integer.
Floating-point evaluation alone gives wrong digit counts for large n; a reproduction must use exact or sufficiently high-precision arithmetic.
The patch is described as partial, so the fix may not cover all cases.
The 857-digit-scale expected literal is only given in the test passage; its full digit string is truncated across passages and must be reassembled exactly.
